rows.citation: Sinha A, Gleeson P, Marin B, et al. (2025). The NeuroML ecosystem for standardized multi-scale modeling in neuroscience. eLife 13:RP95135.
rows.model_type: NeuroML v2 / LEMS models at multiple scales (channels, cells, networks); ecosystem/standards overview
rows.controlled_mutations: no - full text describes schema/LEMS validation, OMV and SciUnit checks; no deliberate fault seeding or mutant generation found.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - ecosystem supports arbitrary LEMS simulations, but the paper proposes no multi-protocol test battery for regression.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - OMV checks outputs such as spike times against tolerance; SciUnit/NeuronUnit cited for feature-level biological validation.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimisation mentioned only for model parameter fitting tools (e.g. BluePyOpt, NeuroTune), not stimulus protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - descriptive ecosystem paper; no held-out models or fault families evaluated.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted editing or transformation of models assessed.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Describes the layered validation cascade NeuroSem would build on (schema, LEMS, OMV tolerance checks, SciUnit). NeuroSem would add seeded single-fault mutants, refinement-calibrated tolerances, multi-protocol fingerprints and greedy battery selection evaluated on held-out models and mutation families.

rows.citation: Gleeson P, Cantarelli M, Marin B, et al. (2019). Open Source Brain: A Collaborative Resource for Visualizing, Analyzing, Simulating, and Developing Standardized Models of Neurons and Circuits. Neuron 103(3):395-411.e5.
rows.model_type: NeuroML v2 / PyNN neuron and circuit models shared on the OSB platform (single cells to networks)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - OMV tests check expected behaviour on each commit; no deliberate fault injection or mutant generation described in full text.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - mep files may list several experiments per model, but no systematic stimulation battery across protocols is proposed.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - expected behaviours such as spike times and resting potential, plus parameter consistency checks, compared within tolerance.

rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Establishes the continuous-integration baseline NeuroSem compares against: fixed per-model expectations with per-simulator tolerances. rows.citation: Marin B, Gleeson P (OpenSourceBrain) (2014). osb-model-validation (OMV): Tools for automated model validation in OpenSourceBrain projects. GitHub repository; PyPI package OSBModelValidation 0.4.0.
rows.model_type: NeuroML v2 / LEMS, PyNN and other models run on multiple simulation engines (jNeuroML, jNeuroML_NEURON, etc.)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - README and analyzer source show expectation-vs-output checks only; no mutant generation or fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - mep/omt files allow multiple named experiments per model; the protocol set is hand-written per project, not a systematic battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - analyzers cover spike times, spike rate, resting potential, input resistance, activation variables, time series, morphology, temperature.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no mechanism to select or minimise experiments/protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - pass/fail regression per model and engine; no held-out evaluation concept.
rows.software: OMV https://github.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation (LGPL-3.0 per GitHub API; PyPI OSBModelValidation 0.4.0, LGPL-3.0-only)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest existing practice and a likely reusable component: tolerance-based regression of recorded observables across simulators on every commit. Tolerances are set by hand per observable. NeuroSem would calibrate tolerances by step refinement, seed controlled mutants, and choose a compact protocol battery validated on held-out models.

rows.citation: Omar C, Aldrich J, Gerkin RC (2014). Collaborative infrastructure for test-driven scientific model validation. Companion Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE Companion 2014), pp. 524-527.
rows.model_type: general scientific models (worked example uses planetary-motion models); framework-level paper
rows.controlled_mutations: no - 4-page paper describes validation tests, capabilities and scores; no fault seeding or mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - tests compare model predictions with observations; no stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no neuroscience features in the paper; domain libraries are envisioned separately.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out evaluation; compares many models against a shared test suite.
rows.software: SciUnit https://github.com/scidash/sciunit (MIT per GitHub API; PyPI sciunit 0.2.8)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Brings unit-testing ideas to validating models against empirical data, scoring goodness of fit. NeuroSem instead tests behaviour preservation between a reference model and its transformed version, adding mutation-calibrated sensitivity and protocol selection. SciUnit could serve as a test harness but does not anticipate the method.

rows.citation: Gerkin RC, Birgiolas J, Jarvis RJ, et al. (2019). NeuronUnit: A package for data-driven validation of neuron models using SciUnit. bioRxiv (preprint).
rows.model_type: single-neuron and ion-channel models, including NeuroML models run via jNeuroML or NEURON backends
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no deliberate model perturbation to measure test sensitivity found in preprint or test source.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - square current injections incl. binary-search rheobase and standard vs strong-stimulus variants of Druckmann-style tests; not a designed battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - about 50 test classes: rheobase, input resistance, resting potential, spike width, latencies, ISIs, accommodation, AHP depth.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimisation (DEAP/BluePyOpt) fits model parameters to test suites; stimulation protocols are not selected or minimised.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out or cross-validation methodology described.
rows.software: NeuronUnit https://github.com/scidash/neuronunit (PyPI neuronunit 0.1.8.2, license MIT per PyPI; GitHub API reports no detected license; last push 2021-07-18)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest feature-level tooling: many electrophysiology tests with rheobase-based stimuli on NeuroML models, scored against experimental data. NeuroSem would instead compare a model against its own reference, calibrate tolerances numerically, seed single-fault mutants, and select a compact battery evaluated on held-out models and mutation families.
